title: Counterfactual Analysis on Large Graphs

problem.claim: Counterfactual analysis seeks minimal, semantically meaningful changes that alter a model's prediction.

gap.claim: Existing perturbation approaches often produce model-dependent explanations detached from the underlying data distribution.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces Counterfactual Subgraph Retrieval, a dataset-grounded formulation that retrieves structurally and semantically similar subgraphs with different predictions under the same model.
It proposes Concept-guided Counterfactual Subgraph Retrieval, which uses a shared multi-scale graph concept space aligned with a trained GNN and performs concept-level reasoning.
The approach combines concept-based filtering, robustness-aware ranking, and diversity-aware selection for scalable, non-redundant search over large graphs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report theoretical guarantees concerning correctness, robustness, and efficiency.
The authors report up to 40% improvement in retrieval quality and 20× speedups on large-scale graphs across six real-world datasets spanning five domains.

narrative_sequence.summary: The work targets counterfactual explanations based on minimal, semantically meaningful changes to model predictions.
Existing node, edge, and attribute perturbations can be model-dependent and disconnected from the data distribution.
The paper formulates counterfactual analysis as retrieval of similar subgraphs that induce different predictions.
CCSGR performs concept-level retrieval using multi-scale graph concepts, filtering, robustness-aware ranking, and diversity-aware selection.
The authors report theoretical guarantees and improvements in retrieval quality and speed across multiple datasets and domains.

source_observation.claim: The method retrieves counterfactual examples from the data distribution instead of constructing them solely through fine-grained edits.

interpretation.claim: Dataset-grounded retrieval may improve semantic validity and verifiability when direct perturbations are poorly aligned with observed data.

application.claim: For graph explanation systems, retrieve concept-level subgraphs with contrasting predictions when domain-valid counterfactuals are important.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach is preferable for domains lacking suitable datasets or concept representations.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the six datasets, five domains, or baseline methods.
The conditions and formal statements of the theoretical guarantees are not provided.
The definitions and evaluation protocols for retrieval quality, robustness, efficiency, and speedup are unspecified.
